description: This command makes inactive all processes other than static mechanical (fluid, thermal, creep, dynamic, etc). Then it solves the static mechanical process till it reaches a convergence of f . If no solve limit is specified then a default limit of ratio 1e-5 is used. At the end of the calculation restore all process settings to what they were at the beginning.

keywords.name: age
keywords.description: Solve until the total model time reaches f. f is an absolute time, not an increment: a model already past f takes one more step and stops.

keywords.name: and
keywords.description: Specify that when multiple solve limits are given, all must be met before cycling is stopped. The default behavior is to stop once any solve limit is met.

keywords.name: calm
keywords.description: Specify that every i cycles, the model will be calmed. For mechanical processes, all velocities (both linear and angular) that are not fixed are nulled during a calm .

keywords.name: cfd
keywords.description: Specifies a solve limit for the cfd process specifically. The process must be active, otherwise the engine reports 'Process cfd is not active'.

keywords.name: clock
keywords.description: Limit the computer run time to f in minutes. By default, there is no limit to the run time.

keywords.name: convergence
keywords.description: Limit based on the maximum convergence value of all gridpoints, zones, structural nodes, balls, clumps, or rigid blocks. The convergence value is defined as the ratio of the current mechanical force ratio to the target force ratio of the gridpoint. See the zone gridpoint initialize ratio-target and structure node initialize ratio-target commands. A convergence value of 1.0 is therefore considered “converged”, but it is possible to restrict or relax that by using a value greater or less than 1.0.

keywords.name: creep
keywords.syntax: creep {cycles <i> | cycles-total <i> | cycles-total-zone <i> | time <f> | time-total <f> | time-total-zone <f>}
keywords.description: Specify a solve limit for the creep process specifically. Options: cycles <i>: Limit of the number of cycles to take with creep active during this solve operation.; cycles-total <i>: Total number of cycles taken with creep active since model creation.; cycles-total-zone <i>: Total number of cycles taken with creep active in the zone module.; time <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active during this solve operation.; time-total <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active since model creation.; time-total-zone <f>: Total accumulated creep time in the zone module.

keywords.name: cycles
keywords.description: Synonym to model cycle .

keywords.name: cycles-super
keywords.description: A solve limit based on the number of “Super-Cycles” taken during the current solve command. One “Super-Cycle” cycle includes all leader and follower steps taken as part of a loosely coupled solve system.

keywords.name: cycles-total
keywords.description: A solve limit based on the total number of accumulated cycles.

keywords.name: dynamic
keywords.syntax: dynamic {cycles <i> | cycles-total <i> | cycles-total-zone <i> | time <f> | time-total <f> | time-total-zone <f>}
keywords.description: Specify a solve limit for the dynamic process specifically. Options: cycles <i>: Limit of the number of cycles to take with dynamic active during this solve operation.; cycles-total <i>: Total number of cycles taken with dynamic active since model creation.; cycles-total-zone <i>: Total number of cycles taken with dynamic active in the zone module.; time <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active during this solve operation.; time-total <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active since model creation.; time-total-zone <f>: Total accumulated dynamic time in the zone module.

keywords.name: elastic
keywords.description: Perform a mechanical calculation in two steps: first, assuming elastic behavior; then, using the actual strength values of the material. The cohesion and tensile strength for all materials in the model are set to high values for the first step. For the second step, the cohesion and tensile strength are reset to their original values. If the optional only keyword is provided, then only the elastic portion (i.e., the first step) is undertaken. This keyword only applies to the mechanical process.

keywords.name: fish-call
keywords.syntax: fish-call <f> <s> [{interval <i> | process {creep | dynamic | fluid | mechanical | thermal}}]
keywords.description: Add the FISH function s to the Fish-Call list at location f , as with the fish callback command. See the section FISH Callback Events for a discussion of FISH callbacks. The following keywords are available to reduce the frequency of the callback. Options: interval <i>: If specified, then the function will only be called every i steps.; process {creep | dynamic | fluid | mechanical | thermal}: If specified, then the function will only be called if the process indicated is active during that particular cycle. Options: creep: The callback will only execute if the creep and mechanical process is active; dynamic: The callback will only execute if the dynamic and mechanical process is active; fluid: The callback will only execute if the fluid process is active; mechanical: The callback will only execute if the mechanical process is active; thermal: The callback will only execute if the thermal process is active. The function is named bare, not quoted: 'model solve fish-call -1 myfunc cycles 10' runs (verified on FLAC3D 9.8 and 7.0); 'myfunc' in quotes fails with 'Bad conversion'.

keywords.name: fish-halt
keywords.description: The FISH function s is called during every cycle to determine whether cycling should continue. If s returns false , cycling continues; otherwise, cycling terminates.

keywords.name: fluid
keywords.syntax: fluid {cycles <i> | cycles-total <i> | cycles-total-zone <i> valid only if FLAC zones exist | ratio-flow <f> FLAC3D only | time <f> | time-total <f> | time-total-zone <f> valid only if FLAC zones exist}
keywords.description: Specifies a solve limit for the fluid process specifically. Options: cycles <i>: Limit of the number of cycles to take with fluid-flow active during this solve operation.; cycles-total <i>: Total number of cycles taken with fluid-flow active since model creation.; cycles-total-zone <i>valid only if FLAC zones exist: Total number of cycles taken with fluid-flow active in the zone module.; ratio-flow <f>FLAC3D only: Specifies a limiting convergence ratio as defined by the fluid-flow logic. See section xxx of the fluid discussion — CS on 3/7/17 still don’t know where this should go; time <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active during this solve operation.; time-total <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active since model creation.; time-total-zone <f>valid only if FLAC zones exist: Total accumulated dynamic time in the zone module.

keywords.name: follower
keywords.description: Make process s (for example mechanical) a follower for this solve: it cycles to equilibrium after each leader step. Give it last, only substep may follow it. Not every active process can be a follower.

keywords.name: mechanical
keywords.syntax: mechanical {convergence <f> | cycles <i> | cycles-total <i> | cycles-total-zone <i> | ratio <f> | ratio-average <f> | ratio-local <f> | ratio-maximum <f> | time <f> | time-total <f> | time-total-zone <f> | unbalanced-maximum <f>}
keywords.description: Specifies a solve limit for the mechanical process specifically. Options: convergence <f>: Limit based on the maximum convergence value of all gridpoints and zones in the model (note that currently PFC balls do not support this keyword). The convergence value for a gridpoint or node is defined as the ratio of the current mechanical force ratio to the target force ratio of the gridpoint. See the zone gridpoint initialize ratio-target and structure node initialize ratio-target commands. A convergence value of 1.0 is therefore considered “converged”, but it is possible to restrict or relax that by using a value greater or less than 1.0.; cycles <i>: Limit of the number of cycles to take with mechanical active during this solve operation.; cycles-total <i>: Total number of cycles taken with mechanical active since model creation.; cycles-total-zone <i>: Total number of cycles taken with mechanical active in the zone module.; ratio <f>: Limit based on the current convergence ratio value, as defined by the various modules that use it. By default this is the same as ratio-average . See ref-equilibrium-.; ratio-average <f>: Limited based on the average convergence ratio. See ref-equilibrium-. This quantity is defined for PFC here .; ratio-local <f>: Limited based on the local convergence ratio. See ref-equilibrium-.; ratio-maximum <f>: Limited based on the maximum convergence ratio. See ref-equilibrium-. CS: Common trouble; time <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active during this solve operation.; time-total <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active since model creation.; time-total-zone <f>: Total accumulated mechanical time in the zone module.; unbalanced-maximum <f>: Limit based on the maximum unbalanced force among model objects.

keywords.name: or
keywords.description: Specify that when multiple solve limits are set, cycling should stop when any one limit is met. This is the default behavior.

keywords.name: ratio
keywords.description: Limit based on the convergence ratio returned by all active modules.

keywords.name: ratio-average
keywords.description: Limit based on the average convergence ratio returned by all active modules.

keywords.name: ratio-local
keywords.description: Limit based on the local convergence ratio returned by all active modules.

keywords.name: ratio-maximum
keywords.description: Limit based on the maximum convergence ratio returned by all active modules.

keywords.name: synchronize
keywords.description: In a typical loosely coupled analysis (most commonly fluid-mechanical) the leader process (fluid) takes one or more cycles and then the follower process (mechanical) cycles to equilibrium. In some cases both processes have timesteps that are meaningful (fluid-thermal coupling, fluid-creep, etc). In which case you can use the synchronize keyword. In this case the follower process(es) will not solve to equilibrium but will instead cycle until the accumulated time matches the time in the leader process.

keywords.name: thermal
keywords.syntax: thermal {cycles <i> | cycles-total <i> | cycles-total-zone <i> | ratio <f> | ratio-local <f> | time <f> | time-total <f> | time-total-zone <f>}
keywords.description: Specifies a solve limit for the thermal process specifically. Options: cycles <i>: Limit of the number of cycles to take with thermal active during this solve operation.; cycles-total <i>: Total number of cycles taken with thermal active since model creation.; cycles-total-zone <i>: Total number of cycles taken with thermal active in the zone module.; ratio <f>: Specifies a limiting convergence ratio as defined by the thermal logic.; ratio-local <f>: Specifies a limiting local convergence ratio as defined by the thermal logic.; time <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active during this solve operation.; time-total <f>: Limit of the time accumulated while this process is active since model creation.; time-total-zone <f>: Total accumulated dynamic time in the zone module.

keywords.name: time
keywords.description: Cycle until the total time accumulated by any active process after the initiation of the solve meets or exceeds f . This is distinct from the time-total keyword that refers to the total age of the process.

keywords.name: time-total
keywords.description: Cycle until the total age of any active process meets or exceeds f . This is distinct from the time keyword.

keywords.name: unbalanced-average
keywords.description: Cycle until the average unbalanced quantity, defined by the active processes, is less than or equal to f . For the mechanical process, unbalanced refers to the average unbalanced force (i.e., the unbalanced force is what remains after all forces are applied to a model object).

keywords.name: unbalanced-maximum
keywords.description: Cycle until the maximum unbalanced quantity, defined by the active processes, is less than or equal to f . For the mechanical process, unbalanced refers to the maximum unbalanced force (i.e., the unbalanced force is what remains after all forces are applied to a model object).

examples.description: Solve the static mechanical process to a convergence of 1

notes: Accepted by the 9.8 PFC, FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint and MassFlow builds; 9.00 and 7.0 reject it.
